correctness.rationale: Direct substitution into Algorithm 1 gives \(s_{1,i}=\gamma h_i x_i\), \(\nu_{1,i}=\gamma h_i^2x_i^2\), and multiplier \(1-q_i\) with \(q_i=c\gamma h_i/(\gamma^{1/3}h_i^{2/3}|x_i|^{2/3}+\varepsilon)\). Since the quadratic is diagonal, objective nonincrease is equivalent coordinatewise to \(0\le q_i\le2\). The supremum of \(q_i\) occurs as \(x_i\to0\), yielding exactly \(c\gamma L\le2\varepsilon\); solving \(q=2\) gives the spike radius, and convex endpoint optimization of \((1-q)^2\) gives the exact supremal factor. Equality at the frontier still gives strict decrease for every finite nonzero active coordinate because its denominator is strictly larger than \(\varepsilon\).

final_claim: For the first practical MADGRAD update from zero accumulators on an axis-aligned positive-definite quadratic, uniform objective decrease for every nonzero initialization holds exactly when \(c\gamma L\le2\varepsilon\); if this fails, the top-curvature coordinate has the stated punctured near-minimizer spike interval and the exact supremal first-step factor \(\max\{1,(c\gamma L/\varepsilon-1)^2\}\).
